recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. Future changes should be tracked against the newer artifact-specific ImagingStudy or Specimen issues rather than reopening FHIR-6240.
issue_request: FHIR-6240 was a Published DSTU1 Imaging Integration change request asking whether multiple identifiers distinguished by identifier.type should be rolled up or kept separate for ImagingStudy and Specimen. Its Not Persuasive with Modification resolution said ImagingStudy AccessionNumber and StudyID have different semantics and are not appropriate to merge, while asking to expand the AccessionNumber description.
initial_application: The Jira comment cites SVN revision 5635, represented in git as 35ce7f52a53f25d5837d69e02d4f31b96045e4b4, which updated the historical ImagingStudy spreadsheet Accession Number short and long descriptions. No FHIR-6240-tagged Specimen hunk was found; later refactors moved the relevant build inputs into current StructureDefinition XML, narrative, examples, search parameter bundles, and fhir.ini migration metadata.
additional_context: ImagingStudy and Specimen are active current-build resources. Later ImagingStudy issues FHIR-22118, FHIR-49675, and FHIR-56033 govern the current accession placement by keeping DICOM Study Instance UID/Study ID on ImagingStudy.identifier and placing accession guidance on ImagingStudy.basedOn.identifier, superseding the temporary contrary direction in FHIR-48644. Later Specimen issues FHIR-44755 and FHIR-53092 intentionally roll accession identifiers into Specimen.identifier using Identifier.type=ACSN and remove the standalone accessionIdentifier element.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. No source hunk is needed because current ImagingStudy source separates accession from the study identifier, and current Specimen source intentionally uses typed identifiers for accession; restoring old prose or adding duplicate guidance would conflict with later final issues or duplicate existing guidance.
